sentences.text:
Jawahar Lal Agrawal vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 August,
2024
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
Cra No. 1421 of 2024

Jawahar Lal Agrawal S/o Late Shri Chandgiram Agrawal Aged About 64 Years R/o Tulsi Marg
Gupta Gali, Korba (C.G.)
 ... Appellant
 versus
State Of Chhattisgarh Through The Station House Officer Ajak Korba, District Korba (C.G.
 ... Respon

14.08.2024 Mr. S.C. Verma, Senior Counsel appears along with Mr. Vikram Sharma, Counsel for the
Appellant.
Mr. Ajit Singh, Government Advocate for the State.
Mr. Malay Shrivastava, appears as an objector.

Heard on admission as well as on I.A. No. 01/2024, an application for suspension of sentence and
grant of bail under Section 430 of Bnss.

By virtue of the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 29.07.2024 in Session Case No. 14/2015, passed by the Special Judge (Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe)
Prevention of Atrocities, Korba, Chhattisgarh , appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction Sentence Section 467 IPC Read Seven years, with fine of Rs. with Section 34 of IPC 14,000/- failing with further imprisonment of seven months.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Section 468 IPC read with Five years with fine of Rs. section 34 of IPC 10,000/- failing with further imprisonment of five months.
Section 471 IPC read with Two years, with fine of Rs. Section 34 of IPC 4,000/- failing with further imprisonment of two months.
Section 3(1)(iv) of SC and Three years along with fine ST Prevention of of Rs. 6,000/- failing which Atrocities Act, 1989 imprisonment of three month R.I.

Learned Senior counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the learned trial court has convicted the present appellant on the ground that, since appellant has purchased the land of Ramsai, at nominal cost of Rs. 50,000/- inspite of their being Market Value of Rs. 10,00,000/- therefore, the appellant cannot said to be a bonafide purchaser, and his conduct shows, that he was aware of the fact, that the land which he was purchasing does not belongs to Seller.

In spite, of the fact that, the same was never the case of the Jawahar Lal Agrawal vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45137952/
1 prosecution and none of the witness has stated this fact.

sentences.text: He further submitted that the compromise took place by and between the parties on which the Trial Court has discharged the accused appellant under Section 419 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code and the appellant was granted anticipatory bail vide MCRCA No. 882/2015 and he was on bail during the entire trial period.

He is having a good case in his favour and balance of convenience also lies in his favour but the appeal is likely to take some more time to be finalized, therefore, it is prayed that his application (I.A. No. 01/2024) may be allowed.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/Respondent has opposed the said application.

Mr. Malay Shrivastava, appearing as an objector also vehemently opposed the prayer made by the learned counsel for the appellant by stating that the fact of compromise is true, but the compromise was done on the basis that the land will be returned back but that has not been done till date.
He further stated that the land which is in the name of some Scheduled tribe person has been purchased by the accused standing some person who is not a member of Scheduled Tribe.
He further submitted that a forged document has been prepared which has been identified by the accused himself.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and also looking to the judgment passed by the Trial Court, the nature of offence and age of the appellant, I am inclined to allow this application without commenting anything on merits of the case.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 01/2024 is allowed and it is directed that the substantive jail sentence imposed upon the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and the appellant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 20,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court .

After being released on bail, he shall appear before the Registry of this Court on 27.09.2024 and thereafter he shall continue to appear before the Trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry on this behalf and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given by the said court till the disposal of this appeal.
In view of above, I.A. No. 01/2024 is allowed and stands disposed of.
List this case for final hearing in its due course.
